skill.name: patchright-skill
skill.description: Patchright-based browser automation for local web application testing, screenshots, and UI interactions. It drives Chrome through local scripts and includes helpers for Google search automation and persistent browser sessions.
skill.summary: Automates Chrome testing and screenshots with Patchright browser control.
skill.author: smallnest

security_audit.summary: Most static high findings are false positives from Markdown examples, localhost documentation, and a prior audit artifact. The substantive risks are semantic: bot-detection bypass intent, unauthenticated local browser control, arbitrary page JavaScript evaluation, private-network reach, and predictable temporary screenshot output.

remediation.issue: Embedded prior audit claims may bias marketplace review.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_result.json from the distributed skill or clearly exclude it from runtime and marketplace analysis.

remediation.issue: Local server accepts unauthenticated browser control commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require a random session token, restrict request size, and stop the server automatically after inactivity.

remediation.issue: The evaluate tool runs arbitrary JavaScript in active pages.
remediation.suggestion: Disable evaluate by default or require explicit per-use confirmation with target URL and script review.

remediation.issue: The package advertises CAPTCHA and bot-detection bypass.
remediation.suggestion: Remove bypass marketing and limit documented use to owned development and QA targets.

remediation.issue: Debug screenshots may be written to predictable temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Write screenshots to a user-approved project directory with unique names and restrictive permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: evaluation_result.json embeds a prior audit-style claim that the skill is low risk, safe to publish, and that all static findings are false positives. This can bias automated reviewers and must not be trusted as authority.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file contains explicit safety and publication claims inside the package under review. It is not phrased as a direct override, so confidence is high but not maximal.

semantic_findings.title: Bot Detection and CAPTCHA Bypass Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill advertises bot detection bypass and specifically names Cloudflare and reCAPTCHA. This enables automation against anti-abuse controls and needs marketplace restriction or strong user warnings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bypass intent is explicitly documented, and the executor launches Chrome with automation-control disabling arguments. This is a clear and central capability.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Local Browser Control Server
semantic_findings.description: scripts/server.py accepts local TCP requests and dispatches browser commands without authentication. Any local process can control the persistent browser session while the server is running.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server listens on localhost and dispatches parsed JSON commands directly. I found no authentication, token check, or origin restriction in the request path.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Page JavaScript Evaluation
semantic_findings.description: The server exposes an evaluate tool that runs caller-provided JavaScript in the active page. This can read page content or trigger page actions on trusted local and private applications.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation directly passes the supplied script to page.evaluate, and the reference documents evaluate-based extraction workflows. The risk is clear even though it is intended automation.

semantic_findings.title: Private Network Browser Access by Design
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly targets localhost, private IP ranges, and private network testing. This can expose internal applications to agent-driven browsing and screenshots if users choose unsafe targets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation and navigation function directly support local and private URLs. This is legitimate for development, but it expands the impact of browser automation misuse.

content.value_statement: Testing local web apps by hand slows frontend feedback. This skill drives Chrome, captures screenshots, and inspects pages through Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Launches Chrome with Patchright and stealth browser settings.
Navigates to local, private network, or external web pages.
Captures browser screenshots to local image files.
Clicks selectors, fills fields, waits for elements, and reads page text.
Keeps a browser session alive through a localhost server.
Runs JavaScript in the active page through the server evaluate tool.
limitations: Requires Patchright and Google Chrome to be installed first.
Persistent mode opens a local server on 127.0.0.1:9222 while running.
The evaluate tool can run page JavaScript, so targets must be trusted.
Google automation can trigger site defenses or violate site terms.

use_cases.title: Check Local UI Changes
use_cases.description: Open a local dev server, interact with components, and capture screenshots after code changes.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Run login, navigation, form, and wait steps in a persistent browser session.

use_cases.title: Verify Pre-Deploy Builds
use_cases.description: Inspect a staged build visually before release and collect page state evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open my local app at port 3000 and capture a full page screenshot named home.png.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the login page, enter test credentials, submit the form, and report the resulting page title.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the dashboard, wait for the data table, extract visible row labels, and save a screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step QA Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a persistent browser session, test the main navigation, capture screenshots after each major step, and summarize failures.

output_examples.input: Capture the login screen on my local app.
output: Opened the local login page successfully.
Reported the visible page title and current URL.

output_examples.input: Fill the email field, submit the form, and check the result.
output: Filled the requested field and clicked the submit button.
Captured the result screen for review.

output_examples.input: Inspect product cards on the current page.
output: Read visible product titles from the page.
Returned the item count and titles.

best_practices: Use this skill only against applications you own or have permission to test.
Stop the local server after each testing session.
Store screenshots in a project folder with appropriate permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not use bot bypass features against third-party sites without authorization.
Do not run evaluate scripts on pages that contain sensitive user data.
Do not leave the persistent browser server running unattended.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Chrome navigation, screenshots, clicks, typing, waits, text extraction, and page evaluation.

faq.question: Does it need a local server?
faq.answer: Persistent sessions use a local server on 127.0.0.1:9222. One-shot executor mode does not keep session state.

faq.question: Can it test localhost applications?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation targets localhost, private IP addresses, and development server ports.

faq.question: Can it browse external websites?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts include Google search helpers, so use them only where automation is permitted.

faq.question: Where are screenshots saved?
faq.answer: Screenshots are saved to paths passed by the user or script, often in the current project or temporary directory.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The evaluate tool and bot-bypass claims require strict use on trusted and authorized targets.
